ACI-WORKFLOW-BINDING-V1:
Alignment audit for SWU-ACI-HOST-BUS-INTEGRITY-001, before any code is written. Read the descriptor at docs/features/agents-communication-infra/work-pack/descriptors/SWU-ACI-HOST-BUS-INTEGRITY-001.json, its context pack and scaffold under work-pack/context/, the parent review at docs/features/agents-communication-infra/reviews/2026-07-25-host-bus-phase-a-close/review.md, and the obligations T-ACI-PHASEA-I1 through I3 in docs/features/agents-communication-infra/TEST-SPEC.md. Then read the current implementations/server/runtime/service.py and the four validation-command test files. Answer exactly: (1) does each of required_changes F4, F5, F6 have a determinate meaning against the accepted Host Binding and BUS contracts, or is any of them underdetermined; (2) for each, name the specific function and condition that must change and the observable that proves it fails closed; (3) does anything in the declared write_scope force a change that would land in one of the explicit_non_goals (F1 invocation-plan authority, F2 producer-output evidence, F3 completion receipt, effect claim, provider or tool execution, ACI-005 materializer, runtime cutover, external network, production); (4) is the declared write_scope sufficient to close F4-F6, or is a file missing. Return PASS only if every required change is determinate, in scope, and free of non-goal contamination. Return a concrete blocking list otherwise. You do not write code and you do not approve your own or the coder's work.

ACI-WORKFLOW-BINDING-V1:
Layering audit for SWU-ACI-HOST-BUS-INTEGRITY-001, before any code is written. Read the descriptor at docs/features/agents-communication-infra/work-pack/descriptors/SWU-ACI-HOST-BUS-INTEGRITY-001.json and then map the module structure of implementations/server/runtime/: which module owns canonicalization, the journal, artifacts, capabilities, host bindings, reveal delivery, the orchestration bridge, and the Stage-E source manifest verification. Answer exactly: (1) for each of F4, F5, F6, which module is the single correct owner of the new check, and does putting it in service.py (the only source file in write_scope) respect or violate that ownership; (2) does F5's requirement to reload and rehash every official peer artifact body introduce a dependency direction that the current layering forbids; (3) does F6's manifest binding of reveal_delivery.py and migration 011 require the verification to live where the manifest is already read, and is that inside write_scope; (4) name any change that would require editing a module outside write_scope to avoid a layering violation. Return PASS only if F4-F6 can be implemented inside write_scope without inverting a dependency or duplicating an existing owner's responsibility. Return a concrete blocking list otherwise. You do not write code and you do not approve your own or the coder's work.

ACI-WORKFLOW-BINDING-V1:
Implement SWU-ACI-HOST-BUS-INTEGRITY-001 (F4, F5, F6) only. You may start only after BOTH alignment auditors have returned PASS; the parent will relay their verdicts to you verbatim because the runtime does not deliver inter-wave input automatically. Write ONLY inside the declared write_scope: implementations/server/runtime/service.py, implementations/tests/runtime/test_host_workflow_binding.py, implementations/tests/runtime/test_bus_reveal_delivery.py, implementations/tests/runtime/test_orchestration_bridge.py, implementations/tests/runtime/aci-test-traceability.json, implementations/tests/runtime/test_aci_traceability.py, and docs/features/agent-provenance-telemetry/integration/stage-e/source-manifest.json. Required changes, verbatim from the descriptor: F4 a follow-up requires a non-empty persisted prior agent_id and exact target equality before any new binding row or event can commit; F5 materialization loads every official peer artifact body and recomputes its digest before trusting stored contribution or reveal hashes; F6 the Stage-E source manifest binds reveal_delivery.py and migration 011, and tamper tests fail closed for both active sources. Add source-linked tests for T-ACI-PHASEA-I1, I2 and I3. Explicit non-goals you must NOT touch: F1 invocation-plan authority, F2 producer-output evidence, F3 completion receipt and status restoration, effect claim, provider or tool execution, the ACI-005 opening materializer, runtime cutover, external network, production. If you change the Stage-E manifest you must also keep STAGE_E_SOURCE_MANIFEST_SHA256 in implementations/server/runtime/local_pilot.py consistent — local_pilot.py is NOT in write_scope, so if that constant must move, STOP and report it as a blocking scope conflict rather than editing it. Run all four validation commands plus the full runtime suite (python -m unittest discover -s implementations/tests/runtime -t .), which was green at 119 tests before you started, and report exact commands and exit results. Inspect your actual diff before reporting. Do not claim completion from prose.

ACI-WORKFLOW-BINDING-V1:
Verify the SWU-ACI-HOST-BUS-INTEGRITY-001 implementation. The parent will relay the coder's task-owned diff, source-linked test results and the pinned input contract to you, because the runtime does not deliver inter-wave input automatically. You never accept prose as evidence. Check exactly: (1) does the diff stay entirely inside the declared write_scope, with no path escape and no edit to implementations/server/runtime/local_pilot.py or host_dispatch_hook.py; (2) does each of F4, F5, F6 have a test that FAILS when the guard is removed, not merely a test that passes with it present — name the test and the mutation for each; (3) for F4, is a null, empty or mismatched prior agent_id actually refused before any binding row or event commits, and is target equality exact rather than partial; (4) for F5, is every official peer artifact body reloaded and rehashed, or does any path still trust a stored hash; (5) for F6, are reveal_delivery.py and migration 011 both bound in the manifest AND do tamper tests fail closed for both; (6) did the full runtime suite stay green at or above 119 tests, and do the four declared validation commands pass with the exact commands recorded; (7) is Stage-E source integrity still PASS, and is the local_pilot manifest self-digest constant still consistent with the manifest on disk. Any failing check returns to the coder within the loop ceiling of 2. Report residual risks explicitly, including anything F4-F6 does NOT protect. You do not approve the dispatch; the final approver is outside every working group.
